intent: The menu row that opens its ContextMenuSub's nested popup.
typical_uses: A row naming a further level of actions, such as Share or Move to

dont_use_when.situation: A row that runs an action directly

invariants.text: While `openOnHover` is on, which it is unless set to false, a mouse pointer resting on the row opens the submenu after `delay` milliseconds (100 when not given) and leaving closes it after `closeDelay` milliseconds (0 when not given); with `openOnHover` false, pressing the row toggles the submenu instead.
The row always ends in a right-pointing chevron; there is no prop to leave it out, and it does not mirror in a right-to-left layout.
context-menu.module.css keeps the row highlighted while its submenu is open.

context-menu.module.css sizes every descendant `svg` of the row to the small icon size and keeps it from shrinking or taking pointer events, so a leading icon passed in children needs no size of its own.
`inset` indents the row's text by the width of the icon column (the small icon size plus two spacing steps), so it lines up with rows that start with an icon.

a11y.by: context-menu.test.tsx asserts the sub-trigger is found by role menuitem and its accessible name, and that clicking it renders the submenu's item inside an element with role menu

onClick.states: onClick is a callback called with the click event when the row is pressed
onClick.because: A React event handler - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the sub-trigger's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the sub-trigger's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (disabled, highlighted, open). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through context-menu.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Rendered by ContextMenuSubTrigger after the children; the kit exposes no prop to replace or hide it.

good.title: A sub-trigger with a leading icon
A sub-trigger that opens only on press

bad.title: A second chevron in the caption
bad.why: The row already renders its own trailing chevron after the children, so the caption's chevron shows as a second one beside it.
